channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [7] Probing picosecond depairing currents in type-II superconductors
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: E. Demler, A. Cavalleri

Authors: E. Wang, M. Chavez-Cervantes, J. Satapathy, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of depairing currents in type-II superconductors, including a cuprate.

Tags: #superconductivity #cuprates #experiment #ultrafast

Abstract: Vortex motion and heating prevent direct-current measurements from reaching the intrinsic depairing limit of type-II superconductors. Picosecond pulses bypass these effects and reveal a sharp threshold in NbN but gradual pair breaking in YBa2Cu3O7.

item.title: [7] Strange metal behaviour from underlying bad metallicity
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Arnaud Ralko, Sergio Ciuchi

Authors: Simone Fratini, Ivan Duchemin, Arnaud Ralko, Sergio Ciuchi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Numerical study on the origin of strange metal behavior, relevant to strongly correlated systems.

Tags: #strangemetal #stronglycorrelated #theory #numerical

Abstract: The origin of the strange metal state is still not known. Now, numerical results suggest that it follows from the quantum statistics of charge carriers, not the temperature dependence of the processes that scatter them.
